title: Console IA + UI patterns for role management, permission warnings, and authz-failure audit visibility (RBAC v2)
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
## Summary
Design the Redwood Console information architecture (IA) and core UI patterns needed for RBAC v2:
1) Role management (view roles, assign roles to members/service accounts)
2) Permission warnings (high-risk permissions + separation-of-duties guidance)
3) Visibility + UX for authorization failures (in-product errors + audit log discoverability)

This ticket targets **default roles** (Org Admin, Billing Admin, Security Admin, Developer, Read-only, Support/Impersonation) and explicitly supports Hosted/Dedicated/Private Console variants.

---

## Background / Why
RBAC v1 is currently coarse and inconsistent. Enterprise customers (Dedicated + Private) expect:
- least privilege + separation of duties
- clear, explainable permission errors
- ability to audit who attempted what (incl. denied actions)

Engineering is implementing RBAC v2 policy evaluation + audit logging. Console needs consistent UX so customers can:
- self-serve admin workflows
- understand/resolve 403s quickly
- avoid insecure misconfiguration (e.g., giving Billing Admin full admin powers)

---

## Goals
- A clear IA that fits existing Console patterns (Org Settings / Project Settings) and scales to enterprise features.
- A role assignment UX that is safe-by-default and minimizes accidental over-privilege.
- Standardized permission warning patterns for “high-risk” actions (P0/P1 from the inventory rubric).
- A consistent 403/unauthorized UX that helps users self-triage and provides required audit context.

## Non-goals (this phase)
- Full custom role editor and permission picker UI (expected later phase; we should leave room in IA).
- Deep SSO/SAML group mapping UI beyond basic “role source” visibility (engineering may expose read-only mapping details).
- Data-plane inference authorization UX (token-level / per-request beyond org/project scopes).

---

## Proposed IA (Console navigation)
### Org-level
**Org Settings → Access**
- Members
- Service Accounts (if not already under Dev Tools)
- Roles & Permissions
- SSO / Identity (existing) (link-outs to role assignment impacts)

**Org Settings → Security**
- Audit Logs (existing/coming)
- Audit Log Export (if applicable)

Rationale:
- “Access” groups the things admins change (people, machines, roles).
- “Security” groups audit and compliance artifacts.

### Project-level
**Project Settings → Access**
- Members (project-scoped membership if supported)
- Service Accounts (project-scoped)

Note: RBAC v2 supports scopes; we should allow UI to show “Org role” vs “Project role” where relevant. If project roles are not in v0, the UI should still be structured to avoid repaint later.

---

## Role Management: UX patterns
### Screen: Roles & Permissions (read-only for most users)
Sections:
1) **Default roles** list (cards or table)
   - Role name
   - Intended audience (e.g., “Finance / billing ops”)
   - Scope (Org / Project)
   - “High-risk permissions included” badge (if any P0)
   - “View details”

2) **Role details drawer/page**
   - Description
   - Permission groups (collapsed by resource: Billing, Org Settings, Projects, API Keys, Dedicated Capacity, Audit Logs, Private Deployment Admin)
   - Explicit callout: “This role can X” in plain language (top 5 human-readable bullets)
   - Technical permission strings (copyable) behind “Advanced” disclosure

Copy guidance:
- Avoid implying customers can edit defaults (for now). Use: “Default roles are managed by Redwood. Custom roles are coming soon.” (if PM approves messaging)

### Screen: Members → Member detail
- Show assigned roles (chips) + scope
- “Change roles” action (only visible if actor has `org.roles.assign` or equivalent)
- “Role source” (Manual / SSO Group / Support session)

### Role assignment modal
Key requirements:
- Explain scope + blast radius upfront.
- Prevent accidental privilege escalation.

Modal layout:
- Member identity (name/email)
- Role selector (single-select for v0; multi-select only if policy supports additive roles)
- Scope selector (Org/Project). If project-scoped not in v0, show disabled with “Coming soon”.
- Warning panel that appears for P0 roles

**P0 warning pattern** (for roles that include any P0 actions):
- Yellow/amber callout with icon + short title: “High-risk access”
- Bullet list of highest risk capabilities (human readable)
- “Separation of duties” note when applicable:
  - Example: Billing Admin should not have Security Admin.
- Optional checkbox: “I understand this grants high-risk access” (Security request; confirm feasibility w/ PM)

Design decision pending: Do we require a typed confirmation (“GRANT”) for the highest-risk roles (Org Admin / Support Impersonation)? Security leaning yes; PM concerned about friction.

### Support / Impersonation role visibility
We need to handle a role that is not intended for customers to assign:
- If present, it should be clearly labeled “Redwood Support (time-bounded)” and non-editable.
- Provide link: “Why am I seeing this?” → help article / tooltip: “Only Redwood Support can enable this during an approved support session. All actions are audited.”

---

## Permission warnings (beyond role assignment)
Places to show warnings:
1) **On pages with high-risk actions** (e.g., API key creation/rotation, SSO settings, audit log export, Dedicated autoscaling)
2) **On buttons/CTAs that trigger high-risk operations**

Pattern tiers:
- **P0 actions**: inline warning + confirm step (modal) + clear audit mention
- **P1 actions**: inline warning only
- **P2**: no warning unless context suggests confusion

Guidance:
- Warnings should not replace permission checks; they are informational.
- Keep warnings consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; wording can vary if feature not available.

Example copy (draft):
- P0: “This change affects org-wide security posture and may impact all projects. This action is recorded in Audit Logs.”

---

## Authorization failures: UX patterns
### In-product error states (403)
Goals:
- Make denied actions self-explanatory and actionable.
- Provide enough context for admins/support without leaking sensitive info.

Standard error components:
- Title: “You don’t have permission to do that.”
- Body: human-friendly explanation (no internal policy jargon)
- Detail row (copyable):
  - Required permission: `org.auditLogs.export` (or similar)
  - Scope: Org / Project + org/project name
  - Request ID / Trace ID (copy)
- CTA: “Contact an Org Admin” (opens small panel with org admins list if user has read access to members; otherwise a generic message)
- Secondary: “View roles & permissions” (links to Roles & Permissions page)

### Disabled controls vs hard errors
- Prefer **disabled controls with tooltip** for navigation and “obvious” restricted actions, to reduce frustration.
- Still handle direct URL/API access with full-page 403.

Tooltip contents:
- “Requires Security Admin role” (role-level guidance)
- Avoid listing the permission string in tooltips; keep that in the 403 details view.

### Audit logs: surfacing denied actions
We need to align with audit log schema changes (ENG-5387): ability to show events with `decision=deny` and reason codes.

Proposed UI additions:
- Audit Logs filter: **Decision: Allowed / Denied**
- Event detail: show
  - Actor
  - Attempted action (human readable)
  - Resource (e.g., project, org)
  - Decision + reason (e.g., “missing permission”, “scope mismatch”, “policy version …”)
  - Correlation ID (ties to 403 request ID)

Open question: should denied actions be visible to everyone who can view audit logs, or only Security Admin? Security prefers Security Admin/Org Admin only. PM to confirm in PRD.

---

## Accessibility + internationalization
- All warning states and error pages must meet contrast requirements.
- Avoid conveying meaning by color alone.
- Keep copy short; permission strings are technical and should be in an “Advanced details” section.

---

## Deliverables
1) IA proposal (sitemap) for Access/Security settings
2) Wireframes for:
   - Roles & Permissions list + role details
   - Member detail + role assignment modal
   - 403 error states (inline + full page)
   - Audit log filters + denied event details
3) Component patterns/spec (callouts, badges, tooltips, confirm modals)
4) Copy doc (draft strings) for PM/Security review

Links (to be attached):
- Figma: Console RBAC v2 – Role management + authz errors (TBD)
- Confluence: RBAC v2 role definitions + overview (see dependencies)

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] IA is approved by PM (Marissa Cole) and Security (Marcus Lin) for v0 scope.
- [ ] Design includes explicit handling for Support/Impersonation role visibility.
- [ ] Standardized 403 UX includes request ID and required permission (advanced) and a clear next step.
- [ ] Audit Logs design includes denied-action filtering and event detail showing decision + reason.
- [ ] Handoff notes include component behaviors and edge cases (no-org-admin-visible, SSO-managed roles, Private deployment feature flags).

---

## Open questions
1) Role model: single role per user vs additive roles? (Impacts modal + display)
2) Should we require explicit confirmation for Org Admin grants? (checkbox vs typed)
3) Should non-admins be able to view Roles & Permissions page (read-only) to understand 403s?
4) Denied audit events visibility: Security Admin only vs broader read-only audit viewers?
5) How do we label “role source” for SSO-managed users in a way that reduces confusion (and reduces support tickets)?

---

## Notes from reviews / comments
### 2025-02-10 (sync w/ Naomi Feldman, Marcus Lin)
- Naomi: prioritize role assignment + 403 UX for GA; custom roles deferred.
- Marcus: strongly prefers explicit separation-of-duties nudges (Billing vs Security).
- Action: incorporate SoD warnings in assignment modal and role details.

### 2025-02-13 (console eng check w/ Chloe Martin)
- Chloe: can support disabled UI + tooltips, but we need a consistent backend signal for “what role/permission is required”.
- Action: keep tooltip generic (role name), show permission string only in 403 details where backend already returns reason codes.

### 2025-02-18 (audit log UX w/ Felix Schneider)
- Align audit log event detail to include `decision_reason` and `policy_version` under Advanced.
- Action: propose an “Advanced” collapsible section in event detail drawer.

---

## Next steps
- Post updated IA + wireframes for review (PM + Security) by 2025-02-21
- Confirm role model constraints with ENG-5386 (single vs multi-role)
- Prepare handoff package for implementation (components + strings) for console sprint planning
